.1 Roth’s comments illustrate a tendency amongst contemporary international lawyers to draw a line between yesterday’s imperialism and today’s international law.2 In contrast, TWAIL scholars have argued against the willed forgetting of international law’s imperial past, and asserted that imperialism is ‘ingrained in international law as we know it today’.3
